question.text: Under Section 15HAA of the SEBI Act, what is the maximum penalty for knowingly altering, destroying, or concealing records required under the Act?

answer.text: Twenty-five crore rupees or three times the profits, whichever is higher
Ten crore rupees or three times the amount of profits made, whichever is higher

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 15HAA prescribes a maximum penalty that can extend to ten crore rupees or three times the amount of profits made out of such act, whichever is higher, for knowingly altering, destroying, mutilating, concealing, falsifying or making a false entry in any record required to be maintained under the Act. The Trap: Twenty-five crore is the maximum for insider trading (Section 15G) and fraudulent and unfair trade practices (Section 15HA), not for record tampering under 15HAA. Note: The "three times profits made" component links the penalty quantum directly to gains derived from the prohibited act.
